rulings.matter: 0 -- what I could check this time that I could not check in RUL-0005
rulings.ruling:
I STILL HAVE NO SHELL AND NO CI ACCESS, AND I FOUND ONE INSTRUMENT I DID NOT USE LAST TIME THAT CHANGES WHAT THIS ADJUDICATION IS WORTH. I state it first because every finding below leans on it and a reader must be able to weigh it.

RUL-0005 refused closure partly because I could not tie any claim to a commit: I said the strings '13900d3' and 'run 58' appeared nowhere in the repository and that my only route to the gate result was the word of the agent that dispatched me. That was true of the working tree. It was not true of .git/logs/HEAD, which is a plain text file, which I can read, and which I did not think to read. It records every movement of HEAD in this repository in order, with parent and child hashes on each line. Reading it, this branch's history is STRICTLY LINEAR across the whole span that matters: each commit's recorded old hash is the previous line's new hash, with no merges anywhere. Ancestry is therefore decidable by position, and I decided it by position rather than by being told.

The relevant sequence, verbatim from that file in order: afbe87f (RUL-0004 lands) -> eb5aa05 'WO-0009 A2: retire the test that certified int overflow as required' -> cd5b1dc 'WO-0008 B1: bound criterion 6 to a domain it can coherently cover' -> 4f4135e 'WO-0008 B2: pin criterion 6's boundary instead of certifying its overflow' -> 13900d3 -> b0dfe2d 'CEO refuses closure: the gate verdict record was never built' -> 4455bfa 'Build the gate-verdict path, which task.schema.json assumed and nobody built' -> 0b3d5c3 -> 83952bb 'The first gate verdict: G2 passes WO-0008 at 0b3d5c3' -> de419a3 -> 490ef24 'G2 passes WO-0009 at de419a3' -> 64567ca 'Rename the boundary test to say what it pins, per RUL-0005' -> 9132222 'File the two records RUL-0005 refused to take on my word' -> 2c6b462 'Re-issue WO-0008's verdict, this time in the order RUL-0005 requires', which is HEAD.

So I can now settle from primary source, and did: that 13900d3 is a real commit rather than a reported one; that ae3169b, the base of the diff RUL-0001 matter 4 named, is a real commit; that 64567ca precedes 9132222; that eb5aa05 precedes 4f4135e; and that every evidence commit cited by every verdict on disk precedes that verdict's own commit. I record what this instrument does NOT give me, because it is the same limitation in a smaller shape: the reflog tells me which commits exist and in what order, and it tells me nothing about what any of them CONTAIN, and it cannot tell me that gate-g2.sh was run or what it returned. Content I checked by reading the working tree. The gate result I address in matter 1 and do not pretend to have re-run.

I record this as an error of mine rather than a discovery. I refused an order in part on 'I cannot check that and I will not pretend otherwise' when a readable file three directories away would have checked most of it. The refusal was still right, for the reason in matter 1, but it was right for a narrower reason than I gave, and a director who overstates its own blindness is doing the same disservice as one who understates it.

rulings.matter: 1 -- is RUL-0005's decisive ground -- that no gate verdict exists -- discharged
rulings.ruling:
YES. THE ARTEFACT EXISTS, IT IS WELL-FOUNDED, AND I VERIFIED ITS WELL-FOUNDEDNESS BY HAND RATHER THAN ASSUMING THE MACHINE HAD DONE IT -- WHICH TURNED OUT TO MATTER.

Studio/state/verdicts/G2-WO-0008-9132222.json: kind gate-verdict, gate G2, taskId WO-0008, commit 9132222, verdict pass, evaluatedAt 2026-08-30T09:17:37Z, evaluatedBy ceo-orchestrator, evidence EVD-0010, EVD-0013, EVD-0014. kernel-manifest.json routes Studio/state/verdicts/*.json to gate.schema.json at layer L2, so the record is schema-governed rather than loose prose in a directory. That is precisely the artefact RUL-0005 said was missing and said would close the order.

WHAT MAKES IT A VERDICT RATHER THAN AN ASSERTION, which is the whole of what I refused last time. Studio/build/emit-gate-verdict.sh takes --gate, --task, --by and --evidence and NO --verdict. I read it. It runs gate-g2.sh, branches on the exit code, and writes pass or fail; there is no argument, environment variable or code path by which it can be told an answer. It refuses any gate but G2 with a message saying another gate needs its own evaluator rather than a flag on this one. It refuses a dirty tree, so the commit the record names is genuinely the tree that was evaluated. And gate.schema.json now requires `commit` on a verdict, with a description saying in terms why: anyone may check that commit out, re-run the gate and contradict the record. THAT is the difference from what I refused in RUL-0005. What I refused was a report -- an agent said a gate passed and asked an adjudicator to transcribe it into a completion field, where the claim would sit unfalsifiable forever. What I have now is a claim bound to a tree that anybody with a shell can destroy. I cannot destroy it myself and I say so in limitations. A claim I cannot personally refute but anyone can is a different kind of object from a claim nobody can refute, and the architecture's demand is falsifiability, not my personal confirmation.

THE FOUR WELL-FOUNDEDNESS RULES, CHECKED AGAINST THIS RECORD ONE BY ONE. KernelCrossCheckTests now carries five extracted predicates -- ClosureIsBackedByAVerdict, CitedEvidenceExists, CoversTheGatesTiers, IsNotSelfIssued, EvidenceIsNotFromTheFuture -- each sprung against synthetic cases in VerdictRuleCases so they cannot pass vacuously, and two live checks that walk the verdict directory. I checked that the synthetic cases are real: they include a closure whose verdict is missing expected false, a gate that never ruled expected false, a cited evidence id that does not exist expected false, a citation missing the T0 tier expected false, and an implementer gating its own work expected false. They are not decorative. But EveryGateVerdictIsWellFounded runs over the verdict directory at the time the suite runs, and this particular verdict was written AFTER the last recorded G2 run and committed at 2c6b462, on which no gate run is recorded. So no machine has yet checked it. I checked it:

(a) Cited evidence exists. EVD-0010, EVD-0013 and EVD-0014 are all on disk under Studio/evidence/tests. Pass.
(b) Covers G2's declared tiers. Studio/constitution/gates.json gives G2 evidenceTiers T0 and T1. EVD-0010 is T0, EVD-0013 is T0, EVD-0014 is T1. Pass.
(c) Evidence is not from the future. EVD-0010 names 4f4135e, EVD-0013 and EVD-0014 name 64567ca, the verdict names 9132222. On the linear history in matter 0, 4f4135e and 64567ca both precede 9132222. Pass. I note the comment on that predicate, which is honest in a way worth recording: it was first written as exact equality, which would have made the rule unsatisfiable in exactly the case it exists for, and the author says plainly it was caught by trying to issue a real verdict rather than by reasoning about one.
(d) Not self-issued. evaluatedBy is ceo-orchestrator; WO-0008's agent is core-simulation-engineer. Pass. I address the weaker half of this in matter 5, because the predicate does not check what I would most want checked.

Condition discharged.

ALL THREE DISCHARGED, EACH CHECKED AGAINST THE TREE AND NOT AGAINST THE BRIEF, WHICH I WAS WARNED TO DO AND WHICH FOUND ONE THING THE BRIEF DID NOT MENTION.

CONDITION 2, A T1 GREEN RUN ON THE FULL TREE -- DISCHARGED. EVD-0014: tier T1, taskId WO-0008, commit 64567ca, verdict pass, 180 Core tests, 185 kernel tests, 0 build warnings, gate-g2.sh reporting G2 PASSED. RUL-0005 refused EVD-0011 not because anything was wrong with it but because it sat at 4f4135e, which predates a change I had ordered to land first. 64567ca IS the rename commit, so this run covers the renamed test rather than merely postdating the order to rename it. The kernel count moving from 162 to 185 is consistent with the twelve synthetic verdict cases and the live checks having been added in the same round, and I checked that the added tests are the ones claimed rather than accepting the count as a number that went up.

CONDITION 3, THE ae3169b DIFF -- DISCHARGED, AND THIS IS THE ONE I CORROBORATED RATHER THAN READ. EVD-0013 records `git diff ae3169b HEAD -- Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateVerificationTests.cs` at 64567ca: one contiguous hunk at @@ -122,33 +122,92 @@, 68 lines added, 9 removed, 2 assertions removed, 10 added, and method-level changes given verbatim. RUL-0001 matter 4 named this diff as a gate step and said in terms it was not claiming it done; RUL-0005 matter 3 made it blocking. It has now been performed and filed. I could not run it myself, so I checked the file it describes against what it claims: RunStateVerificationTests.cs today has Criterion3_PositiveInfinityDtThrowsAndLeavesStateUnchanged and Criterion3_NaNDtThrowsAndLeavesStateUnchanged where the -Increments pair used to be; it has the added Criterion3_ManyTicksWithVariedDt_NonFiniteEntriesThrowAndDoNotIncrement; and Criterion3_ManyTicksWithVariedDt survives under its own name with dtValues = { 0f, 0.1f, 1000f, float.MaxValue } -- finite entries only, which is exactly the split criterion 8 permits in its own words. That is the three founder-authorised inversions plus the added regression test plus the authorised split and nothing else, and the two removed assertions being the inversions themselves is the arithmetic the founder's authorisation predicts. The file agrees with the record. That is corroboration and not proof, and I grade it as such below.

CONDITION 4, THE RENAME BEFORE THE VERDICT -- DISCHARGED, AND ON THE TIMING, NOT MERELY ON THE FACT. Criterion6_OverflowPossibilityNote is gone; WO0008CriteriaVerificationTests.cs:306 is Criterion6_ExactSumAtMaxValueIsFiniteAndExact. I read the body: two ticks of float.MaxValue / 2f, then Assert.That(float.IsFinite(...), Is.True) and Assert.That(elapsedAfter, Is.EqualTo(float.MaxValue)). Unchanged from what RUL-0005 examined; the rename touched the identifier and nothing else, which is what RUL-0004's precedent for Criterion10_MultipleFairingPaths requires of a rename. The name now states what the test pins instead of the opposite of it, which was the entire complaint. I deliberately did not dictate the string in RUL-0005 and I will not second-guess it now beyond saying it does the job.

AND THE TIMING, WHICH WAS THE WHOLE POINT OF MAKING IT BLOCKING. The reflog puts 64567ca ('Rename the boundary test to say what it pins, per RUL-0005') immediately before 9132222, and the operative verdict names 9132222. The rename landed inside the order and before the verdict that closes it, not afterwards on the strength of a paragraph. That is what I asked for and it is what happened.

rulings.matter: 3 -- the premature verdict at 0b3d5c3: was leaving it right, and does it taint the re-issued one
rulings.ruling:
LEAVING IT WAS RIGHT, IT DOES NOT TAINT THE RE-ISSUED ONE, AND I WOULD HAVE RULED AGAINST DELETING IT IF IT HAD BEEN DELETED. I take the second question first because it is the one closure turns on.

DOES IT TAINT. No, and the reason is that the two records make different claims and both are true. G2-WO-0008-0b3d5c3.json says: G2 was evaluated against commit 0b3d5c3 and passed, citing EVD-0010 and EVD-0011. Nothing in that sentence is false. G2 did pass at 0b3d5c3 -- the studio has EVD-0011's green run at 4f4135e and a G2 run at 64567ca on either side of it, and 0b3d5c3 sits between them on a linear history containing no change to Assets/Core. What was premature was not the verdict but its SUFFICIENCY FOR A PURPOSE: it evaluated a tree that did not yet carry a change RUL-0005 had ordered to land before the verdict was taken, so it could not be the verdict that closes WO-0008. A verdict is a statement about a commit. It is not a statement that an order is ready to close; that judgement is a director's and it is being made here, now, against 9132222. A true statement about an earlier tree cannot contaminate a true statement about a later one, and closure below cites 9132222 by name so no reader has to guess which.

WAS LEAVING IT RIGHT. Yes, and the author's own reason is the right one, stated in the brief as 'removing it would make the sequence look tidier than it was'. I endorse that and I will put it more strongly, because it is a principle this studio should be able to reuse. This ruling's own predecessor, RUL-0007 matter 3, refused to edit RUL-0002 and RUL-0003 to repair a renumbering that had made their grades false as read, on the ground that a ruling is a judgement at a point in time and the record is corrected by adding to it, never by rewriting it. The same rule governs a verdict, and more forcibly: a verdict's entire claim to authority is that it reports what a run returned. A studio that deletes true records when they become inconvenient to its narrative has a record that describes intentions rather than events, and the first thing it will delete under pressure is a failing one. The distance between 'remove the premature pass because it is untidy' and 'remove the failing run because it was a fluke' is one step, and the step is taken by whoever establishes that records may be removed for how they look.

So: the record stays, this ruling names it as superseded for the purpose of closing WO-0008 and not as false, and the reason it was superseded is on the record next to it.

ONE CONSEQUENCE I MUST NAME BECAUSE THE AUTHOR DID NOT, AND IT IS THE ONE THING IN THIS PASS I NEARLY MADE BLOCKING. There are now two pass verdicts for WO-0008 on disk, and task.schema.json's completedByGate is a GATEID -- 'G2' -- not a verdict id and not a commit, and the record is additionalProperties: false, so the order file has nowhere to say WHICH verdict closed it. The cross-check EveryCompletedTaskIsBackedByAGateVerdict matches on the pair (gate, taskId), so with two verdicts present it cannot distinguish them, and it would be satisfied by either. Today nothing turns on that: both are pass, the later one is strictly better founded, and this ruling names it. But the shape is wrong, and it will be wrong in a way that matters the first time an order accumulates a pass at one commit and a FAIL at a later one -- the check will find the pass and be satisfied while the tree is red. I am not holding a finished order for it, because the defect is in a check rather than in this delivery and it does not make today's closure unsafe. It is mine, it is the lead architecture item behind the digest, and I have recorded the reasoning here rather than only in a nonBlocking line so that whoever fixes it inherits the argument and not just the instruction.

YES. I CLOSE IT, AND I WANT THE GROUND STATED PRECISELY BECAUSE I REFUSED THIS SAME ORDER THIS MORNING AND A DIRECTOR WHO REVERSES WITHOUT SAYING WHY CHANGED IS JUST WEATHER.

RUL-0005 found the engineering finished and refused on machinery: the last link in the chain of custody had never been built, so completedByGate would have pointed at nothing and 'a gate said so' would have meant 'an agent said so and an adjudicator wrote it down'. Every one of the four conditions I set is now discharged against the tree -- the verdict exists and is well-founded (matter 1), the T1 run covers the whole tree including the rename (matter 2), the diff RUL-0001 named two rulings ago has finally been performed and filed (matter 2), and the rename landed before the verdict rather than after it (matter 2). Nothing was engineered around and nothing was cleared by my reading a file that a previous director had already said reading would not clear.

WHAT CHANGED IS NOT THAT I HAVE BECOME MORE TRUSTING. It is that the thing I was asked to trust has been replaced by a thing that can be contradicted. In the morning I was asked to write a completion field on the strength of a sentence in a dispatch; now there is a schema-governed record naming a commit, produced by a script that has no way to be told an answer, citing evidence that exists, covering the gate's declared tiers, descending from every commit it cites, and issued by someone other than the agent whose work it measures. If it is false, checking out 9132222 and running ./Studio/build/gate-g2.sh exposes it. That is the standard the architecture actually sets. It does not set the standard 'the adjudicator personally observed the run', and it could not, since no adjudicator observes CI either.

I RECORD WHAT CLOSURE DOES NOT MEAN, in the same terms RUL-0003 matter 5 warned about, because 'recorded as closed when it was not' is this studio's recurring failure and its cousin is 'closed and therefore beyond question'. Closing WO-0008 asserts that its twelve criteria are met on the evidence graded below and that G2 passed on a named tree. It does not assert that the code is beyond challenge, it does not retire the non-blocking findings carried below, and it does not make the verdict unfalsifiable -- if someone re-runs G2 at 9132222 and it is red, that is a challenge with evidence and it will be heard, and this ruling will have been wrong rather than final.

Writing status 'completed', completedByGate 'G2' and completedAt into Studio/orders/open/WO-0008.json, changing nothing else in the file. The verdict that backs it is Studio/state/verdicts/G2-WO-0008-9132222.json.

rulings.matter: 5 -- the residual weakness in the new path, stated by me rather than left for someone else to find
rulings.ruling:
THE EVALUATOR AND THE ADJUDICATOR ARE THE SAME ACTOR, NOTHING MECHANICAL PREVENTS THAT, AND I AM NOT GOING TO CLOSE AN ORDER ON A NEW PATH WITHOUT WRITING DOWN ITS WEAKEST JOINT.

IsNotSelfIssued compares the verdict's evaluatedBy against the ORDER'S AGENT. That is the right invariant and it is the one that matters most -- an implementer may not gate its own work, and here it does not: core-simulation-engineer wrote the code, ceo-orchestrator ran the gate. But it does not compare evaluatedBy against the director who then rules on closure, and in this round those are one actor. The executive built the closure path, ran the gate, filed the verdict, and is now ruling that the verdict is good enough to close the order.

I defend it as far as it goes and no further. It is defensible because RUL-0005 ruled that designing the closure path is an architecture decision and therefore mine, so building it inside my own division is not a trespass; because the emitter cannot be told an answer, so running it is not the same kind of act as writing a conclusion; and because the record names a commit, which means my ability to influence the outcome ends at the point where anyone else can re-run it. It is nonetheless weaker than an independent evaluator, and the honest statement of the residue is this: the new path removes 'an agent's word' as the basis of a verdict, and it does not yet remove concentration of roles. Separation of evaluator from adjudicator is the next thing to build, alongside the verdict-pointer defect in matter 3, and I am naming both here so that neither depends on my remembering them.

I also record, against my own convenience, that the founder asked for these orders closed and I am now closing them one pass after refusing. That sequence is exactly the shape a captured adjudicator would produce, and the only thing distinguishing it from capture is that the conditions were written down in advance, in public, and were discharged one by one with artefacts anyone can inspect. That is why RUL-0005 spelled them out rather than refusing in general terms, and it is the reason this ruling can be checked rather than merely believed.

criteriaAssessment.notes: The single change from RUL-0005's assessment is criterion 8, which moves from notYetEvidenced to satisfiedByEvidence on EVD-0013. That was the grade RUL-0005 recorded as harsher than RUL-0001's, on the ground that its closing clause -- 'No other existing assertion in this file is altered' -- is a claim about a diff and is checkable no other way, and that reading is not diffing. The diff has now been run and filed. I grade it satisfiedByEvidence rather than satisfiedByInspection deliberately: my own contribution was to read RunStateVerificationTests.cs and confirm it says what EVD-0013 claims it says, which corroborates the record and is not a substitute for it, and the record is what carries the grade. Criterion 11 is now evidenced by EVD-0014 at 64567ca rather than by EVD-0011 at 4f4135e; EVD-0011 is not withdrawn and remains true of the tree it names, it is simply no longer the operative record for this criterion. Criterion 6 stays satisfiedByEvidence and stays out of unsatisfiableAsWritten for the reason RUL-0005 matter 5 gave at length: the specification defect was cured by its author on RUL-0001's terms, in the direction of narrowing a domain rather than narrowing a safety claim, and the renamed boundary test pins the amended bound from the safe side. Criteria 1-5, 9, 10 and 12 remain ADOPTED from RUL-0001 via RUL-0005 and are still not independently re-derived; nothing in this round touched Assets/Core/Run/RunState.cs and I have no new information about them. I say so rather than implying a fuller review than I performed, for the third ruling running.

nonBlockingLogged: THE VERDICT POINTER IS AMBIGUOUS BY CONSTRUCTION. completedByGate is a gateId, the order record is additionalProperties: false, and two pass verdicts for WO-0008 now exist. EveryCompletedTaskIsBackedByAGateVerdict matches on (gate, taskId) and cannot tell them apart. Harmless today because both are pass and this ruling names the operative one; wrong the first time an order carries a pass at one commit and a fail at a later one, when the check will find the pass and be satisfied while the tree is red. Reasoning in full at matter 3. Mine, and the lead architecture item.

THE EVALUATOR AND THE ADJUDICATOR ARE THE SAME ACTOR AND NO CHECK NOTICES. IsNotSelfIssued protects against the implementer gating its own work, which is the invariant that matters most and which holds here. It does not separate whoever ran the gate from whoever rules on closure. Matter 5. Mine, and it goes with the item above rather than separately.

G2-WO-0008-9132222.json HAS NOT YET BEEN MACHINE-CHECKED. It was written after the last recorded G2 run and committed at 2c6b462, on which no gate run is recorded, so EveryGateVerdictIsWellFounded has never seen it. I checked its four rules by hand in matter 1 and all four hold. The next G2 run will check it mechanically, along with the two closures filed today. Not a reason to hold a finished order, and stated so nobody later mistakes my hand check for a machine one.

MY OWN TIMING ARGUMENT IN RUL-0005 MATTER 4 RESTED ON A FALSE PREMISE, AND I CORRECT IT AGAINST MYSELF. I wrote that Assets/Tests/Core.Tests 'is inside no open order's scope' the moment WO-0008 closes. WO-0010 is open and its writeScope is Assets/Core/** and Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/**, so the file does not leave every open order's scope today. The disposition was still right, for a better reason than the one I gave: a verdict must evaluate the tree the ruling required, and the premature verdict at 0b3d5c3 is the demonstration -- it passed on a tree that did not carry the ordered rename, which is precisely why it could not be the closing one.

The three Console.WriteLine calls in Criterion6_ExactSumAtMaxValueIsFiniteAndExact survive the rename. Harmless. Carried from RUL-0005 unchanged and still not worth a round; the file remains inside WO-0010's write scope, so the opportunity to remove them under an authorisation has not been lost, contrary to what RUL-0005 implied.

boundariesObserved: I wrote no production code and no test code and touched nothing under Assets/**. I amended no acceptance criterion and authorised no amendment; WO-0008's twelve criteria are byte-for-byte as RUL-0005 found them and I re-read them to be sure before grading. I did not edit Studio/build, the kernel schemas, the constitution, CI, LESSONS.md, any proposal's status, or any prior ruling -- including RUL-0005, whose matter 4 I have found rested on a false premise and which I corrected by adding to the record here rather than by rewriting it there, which is the rule RUL-0007 matter 3 bound me to and which I would want held against me. I did not delete, move or alter Studio/state/verdicts/G2-WO-0008-0b3d5c3.json, and matter 3 rules that nobody else should either. In Studio/orders/open/WO-0008.json I wrote exactly the three fields I was authorised to write -- status, completedByGate, completedAt -- and changed nothing else. I did not run the gate, did not override it, and did not sign it; I ruled that a record of someone else having run it meets the standard I set, which is adjudication and not evaluation. I did not re-derive the eight criteria adopted from RUL-0001 and said so rather than implying I had. I did not escalate: the founder asked for closure, I am granting it on conditions I set publicly one pass earlier, and nothing here touches the pillars, the non-goals, an irreversible action, monetisation or player data. I filed no proposal and no challenge, and matters 3 and 5 name two defects in machinery I own rather than routing them at anyone else.
whyNoChallenge: Nothing is violated and nothing was concealed. RUL-0001 found the implementation correct across every criterion it could reach, RUL-0005 found all four of its conditions discharged, and this round discharges the four I added -- with artefacts, not assurances. The one thing in the brief that invited a finding against the author, the premature verdict at 0b3d5c3, is ruled in matter 3 to be a true record that was reported to me unprompted, superseded rather than false, and correctly left on disk; charging an agent for volunteering a sequencing error it had already corrected would teach the studio to stop volunteering them, which is the last lesson this record needs. The two defects I did find -- an ambiguous verdict pointer and no separation between evaluator and adjudicator -- are in machinery RUL-0005 ruled was mine to design, and a director challenging its own architecture is theatre where a ruling and a digest item are the honest instruments.
limitations: I have no shell, no git and no CI access. My instruments were reading the working tree, searching it, and reading .git/logs/HEAD, which I had not used in RUL-0005 and which is why several things I called uncheckable then are checked now. Five consequences, stated rather than glossed. First and most important: I DID NOT RUN gate-g2.sh AND CANNOT CONFIRM ITS EXIT CODE AT 9132222. I read the emitter and satisfied myself that it cannot be told an answer, and I verified everything about the resulting record that is verifiable from inside the repository, but the proposition 'G2 passed at 9132222' rests on that script having been run as the record says. What has changed since RUL-0005 is not that I can now confirm it -- it is that the claim now names a tree, so anyone with a shell can refute it, and a claim that can be refuted is a different object from one that cannot. Second, the reflog tells me which commits exist and in what order and nothing about their contents; the linearity finding in matter 0 is only as good as that file, and if history were rewritten after these entries the ordering would be stale, though the entries I rely on are all recent and consecutive. Third, I could not run the ae3169b diff, so EVD-0013 carries criterion 8 and my reading of RunStateVerificationTests.cs corroborates it; the file agreeing with the record is weaker than having produced the diff and I graded it accordingly. Fourth, my grading of criteria 1-5, 9, 10 and 12 is adopted from RUL-0001 through RUL-0005 and inherits whatever that reading was worth; RUL-0001 was itself produced without a shell. Fifth, I verified that no CI-authored record can exist in this repository by reading .github/workflows/gate-g2-code.yml, which uploads evidence as an artifact rather than committing it; that reading governs matter 1 of RUL-0009 and I record it here too because the same fact underwrites both closures.
